title: Durable ProductContractRevision writer and full-revision store reader composing the landed core codec
description:
FILED BY architect-a69740e0 on 2026-08-28 at governor-0af24e35's explicit 17:59Z request ("both need a row FILED INTO PLANNING, and I do not create rows"). Measured independently at HEAD 3c23339a; the governor's numbers reproduce exactly.

THE LONGEST DEAD CHAIN ON THE BOARD. This gates task-db1a8566958f416b92105cc2c7e51591 (P2.10a) -> task-8e62300ce177 (P2.10b) -> task-c289b8fb (the terminal PR#3 acceptance row). Nothing in that chain moves until this exists. architect-94dd67c9 ruled at 09:56Z that a prerequisite production writer+reader slice was required rather than a narrowed resolver DoD, then that seat died without filing it — the gap has been unowned for ~8 hours.

MEASURED, symbol by symbol, at HEAD 3c23339a. `git grep -n "createProductContractRevision|decodeProductContractRevisionBytes" HEAD -- packages apps`, excluding tests, returns exactly FOUR lines and not one is a call site:
- packages/core/src/product-contract/product-contract-codec.ts:78 — the `createProductContractRevision` DEFINITION
- packages/core/src/product-contract/product-contract-codec.ts:116 — the `decodeProductContractRevisionBytes` DEFINITION
- packages/core/src/index.ts:129 — the barrel RE-EXPORT
- packages/core/src/index.ts:144 — a doc comment naming the seam
Positive control: `git grep -c export HEAD -- product-contract-codec.ts` returns 11, so the probe runs and the zero-call-site result is proven rather than assumed.
There is no revision EVENT, no schema, no durable BYTES, and no full-revision STORE READER. task-db1a8566's approval writer admits only a shape-only ref.

THE PURE HALF ALREADY EXISTS — COMPOSE IT, NEVER REIMPLEMENT IT. `packages/core/src/product-contract/` is a complete pure slice, all tracked at HEAD with `.js` bridges: product-contract-codec (create :78, `deriveProductContractRevisionDigest` :94, `encodeProductContractRevision` :102, decode :116, `PRODUCT_CONTRACT_DIGEST_DOMAIN` :21), plus product-contract-admission, product-contract-lineage, product-contract-materiality, product-contract-acceptance-binding and product-contract-contract. This row adds the DAEMON-SIDE DURABLE SLICE around that codec: an event type, the committed bytes, and a reader that returns a FULL revision. A second codec, a second digest derivation, or a local re-validation of what the core already validates is a competing authority and is forbidden.

WHY IT CANNOT BE SKIPPED OR MOCKED. task-db1a8566's blockedReason states it: without a durable revision, "a positive resolver arm would validate caller/reference bytes or a hand-built fixture, fabricating revision existence and digest authority." Epic rail 4 forbids a mock-only P1 boundary, so narrowing the resolver's DoD is not an option and neither is a fixture standing in for the writer.

RAIL 8(B) — THIS ROW MUST REGISTER ITS CONSUMER EDGE. The governor named the exact failure this board keeps paying for: "A codec that exists and is called by nothing satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist." task-965cb2d6 burned 26 claim-and-release cycles because createGoalWithSource landed with no importer; the cutover reducer shipped at 09dc68d4 needed task-b8272ee0 filed just to register it. The pure-package clause admits either form: NAME the consuming task and record its id, or land the consuming call site here. task-db1a8566 is the named consumer — record that id, and prefer landing at least one durable call site if it fits the path cap.

OWNERSHIP AT FILING: re-measure at claim; this board carries heavy foreign WIP. Probe existence with `git grep <pat> HEAD -- <paths>` or `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>` and NEVER with `git log --oneline -1 -- <path>`, which prints nothing and EXITS 0 on an untracked path. Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` immediately before the gate and quote that sha beside every grep — HEAD moves several times an hour here and a stale-sha gate has already produced one false block today.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, recorded in a row comment (not the completion summary, which is write-only and persists nowhere). Re-capture `git rev-parse HEAD` and quote it beside every probe. Confirm the gap still holds: `git grep -n "createProductContractRevision\|decodeProductContractRevisionBytes" HEAD -- packages apps` excluding tests still shows ONLY definitions and the barrel re-export, with a positive control proving the probe ran. If a production call site now exists, ADOPT and verify it rather than building a second slice, and report blocked as duplicate.

A durable ProductContractRevision is COMMITTED by a production writer through the store's expected-version decision path, carrying bytes produced by the LANDED core codec — `createProductContractRevision` and `encodeProductContractRevision` are composed, never reimplemented, and the digest comes from `deriveProductContractRevisionDigest` rather than a local hash. A second codec or digest derivation is a competing authority and fails this item.

A production READER returns a FULL revision from the store — not a shape-only ref — decoding through `decodeProductContractRevisionBytes` and forwarding that decoder's own refusal code and layer unchanged on malformed bytes. An arm proves a revision written by the writer reads back byte-identical through the reader, over a real file-backed SQLite store with close-and-reopen.

Refusals assert the EXACT stable reason code AND the refusing layer, never merely that the call failed. Before choosing any code, grep the runtime error registry for which codes admit the aggregate this slice uses: `createRuntimeError` returns UNKNOWN_ERROR and DOES NOT THROW when a code is unknown or the descriptor does not list the aggregate, so a wrong code compiles, runs, refuses, and silently loses its identity while every 'it refused' arm stays green. Include a dedicated arm asserting no refusal this slice produces has code UNKNOWN_ERROR.

RAIL 8(B) CONSUMER EDGE: the row records task-db1a8566958f416b92105cc2c7e51591 as the named consumer in a row comment, and — preferably — lands one durable call site so the reader is composed rather than merely exported. 'Exports the symbols' is not composition, and a slice nothing imports satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

Replay and conflict are proven, not asserted: an identical write is byte-identical and adds ZERO decision and ZERO event rows (assert the row COUNTS with denominators), and a same-identity/different-bytes retry refuses deterministically with an exact code and layer.

Mutation drills, each reddening a NAMED arm: bypass the core codec and hand-build the bytes -> the compose arm reds; return a shape-only ref from the reader -> the full-revision readback arm reds; change one refusal's source aggregate to one the descriptor does not list -> the anti-UNKNOWN_ERROR arm reds. Restores proven by `git diff --exit-code` for tracked paths and by SHA256 against an out-of-tree %TEMP% backup for any new file, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A green drill is a FINDING to report, never a pass to bank.

Gates standalone, foreground and unpiped with nonzero counts: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0 quoting its `$ tsc` echo, and the focused daemon suite quoting its `Test Files`/`Tests` count lines — the root vitest include has NO apps/**, so a bare `pnpm test` runs zero daemon tests. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base versus HEAD with an EMPTY owned-path intersection; every production file under 400 lines and targeting 250; every new `.ts` accompanied by its `.js` bridge; explicit-pathspec commit.
taskRails: COMPOSE the landed core slice at packages/core/src/product-contract/**; never reimplement its codec, its digest derivation, or its admission. A second derivation that agrees today drifts tomorrow, and a drifted revision digest binds authority to a revision nobody else can find.

Never fabricate revision existence or digest authority. If the durable revision cannot be produced honestly at some point in the path, report the measured prerequisite — a fixture or caller-supplied bytes standing in for the writer is precisely what task-db1a8566 blocked on, and epic rail 4 forbids a mock-only P1 boundary.
This row lands the producer slice. It does NOT narrow, re-plan or satisfy task-db1a8566's resolver DoD — that row consumes this one and certifies its own boundary.

Register the consumer edge (Rail 8(B)): name task-db1a8566 and record its id, and prefer landing one durable call site. A codec called by nothing passes every existence grep while the feature does not exist — this board has paid for that three times.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement the minimum durable writer in product-contract-revision-store.ts and its one-line `.js` bridge. Export a typed `commitProductContractRevision(store, input)` production surface plus the domain event/schema/address helpers needed by the sibling reader; keep writer refusal-layer constants private.

The input carries projectId, principalId, correlationId, decidedAt, and an unknown draft. Call bare @moe/core `createProductContractRevision(draft)`; forward any core refusal object unchanged. Call `deriveProductContractRevisionDigest(created.revision)` and use that returned digest for the ProductContractRevisionRef/result; forward refusal unchanged. Call `encodeProductContractRevision(created.revision)` and use its exact Uint8Array as requestBytes, committedResultBytes, and the single `ProductContractRevisionCommitted` event payload; forward refusal unchanged. Do not JSON.stringify, hash revision content, or revalidate locally.

Derive a bounded domain-separated address from projectId+contractId+revisionId only (never call it revisionDigest), and derive deterministic aggregate/command/event IDs from that address. Commit the internal decision kind `product-contract.revision.commit` at expectedVersion 0 with `domainSchemaVersion: PRODUCT_CONTRACT_VERSION`. The digest is intentionally not part of the decision identity: changed content for the same identity must meet the same key and conflict, while identical canonical bytes replay. Require EFFECTS_COMMITTED for success; return DECIDED/REPLAYED with the full revision, ref, and exact bytes. Catch DurableStoreError and forward its stable code at `DURABLE_STORE`; map only an unexpected storage failure fail-closed via a correctly sourced `createRuntimeError({code:'STORAGE_DEGRADED', source:{aggregate:'PROJECT', state:'DEGRADED'}})` and never synthesize a competing codec/store code.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented the planned minimum writer and one-line Node bridge. The production surface composes bare @moe/core create -> derive -> encode, commits the exact canonical bytes as request/result/event through expectedVersion 0 under a domain-separated project+contract+revision address, omits digest from decision identity, requires EFFECTS_COMMITTED, forwards DurableStoreError at DURABLE_STORE, and maps only unexpected failures through the registry-admitted STORAGE_DEGRADED PROJECT/DEGRADED source. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` executed `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json`; its only diagnostic is the expected step-3 missing reader import in the red test (TS2307 at line 16). No writer diagnostic was emitted. Focused suite remains deliberately red until the reader exists.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement the full reader in product-contract-revision-reader.ts and its one-line `.js` bridge. Export `readProductContractRevision(store, {projectId, ref})`, consume the writer's aggregate/event helpers, and read the exact aggregate through the store port. Keep reader layer/constants private; do not add daemon-root exports or runtime vocabulary.

Fail closed on zero events, more than one event, wrong eventType/domainSchemaVersion, and decoded contractId/revisionId/revisionDigest disagreement with the requested ref, using distinct stable reader codes and the private reader layer. After count/type/schema checks, pass the stored payload directly to bare @moe/core `decodeProductContractRevisionBytes`; if it refuses, return that exact ProductContractRefusal object without changing its code or `PROVENANCE` layer. On success return the full decoded ProductContractRevision and byte-identical payload, never a ref-shaped projection and never a second validation/encoding/digest calculation.

For a DurableStoreError, forward its exact code at DURABLE_STORE. For an unexpected read failure, create STORAGE_DEGRADED with the runtime registry's admitted PROJECT/DEGRADED source and return its code at the reader layer. Close/reopen ownership remains with the caller/test harness; the reader must be side-effect free and leave raw decision/event counts unchanged.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented the planned full reader and one-line Node bridge. amendments.description:
STEP 5 (AMENDED) — GIVE THE READER ITS OWN SUITE, THEN GATE AND COMMIT.

OWNED PATHS: SIX. `amend_plan_step` cannot write `affectedFiles`, so THIS TEXT is the authorization and supersedes that field, which lists five. The sixth is NEW: apps/daemon/src/product-contract/product-contract-revision-reader.test.ts. Every one of the five existing untracked files is PRESERVED; nothing is deleted.

WHY THE GATE REDS, measured at HEAD 62b4d7f6 so nobody re-derives it. runtime-entrypoint.test.ts:185 "has an exact .js bridge for every runtime module and none for test-tier ones". Its tier function at :160 seeds from `file === ENTRY_MODULE || present.has(testSiblingOf(file))` and then walks `relativeImportTargets(file)` over `modules` — a list that EXCLUDES `.test.ts`. So an import FROM a test file never propagates the tier.
  `product-contract-revision-store.ts` HAS a `.test.ts` sibling -> runtime tier -> its bridge is expected. Correct today.
  `product-contract-revision-reader.ts` has NO sibling, and the only importer is store.test.ts:16 -> it stays TEST-tier -> its `.js` bridge appears in the gate's `unexpected` list. That is the red.

THREE FIXES WERE POSSIBLE. Take the third.
  (i) DELETE the reader bridge — rejected: store.test.ts:16 imports `./product-contract-revision-reader.js`, so removing it breaks loadability, and the human unblock forbids it.
  (ii) MAKE THE PRODUCTION STORE IMPORT THE READER — rejected, and this is the important one. The writer has no need of the reader; adding the edge purely so the tier walk reaches it is a writer->reader cycle that games the scanner. The gate would go green while the topology it certifies became a lie. The human unblock names this explicitly.
  (iii) SPLIT THE READER'S ARMS INTO ITS OWN SIBLING SUITE — take this. It is honest because THE ARMS ALREADY EXIST AND ALREADY TEST THE READER; they are merely in the wrong file, which is precisely why the sibling is absent.

(a) CREATE apps/daemon/src/product-contract/product-contract-revision-reader.test.ts and MOVE the reader-owned arms out of product-contract-revision-store.test.ts (300 lines). Measured, the arms to move:
  :194 the byte-identical READBACK over a real file-backed store with close-and-reopen (DoD 3)
  :238, :248, :264 the ref/identity refusal arms
  :270-271 the `["reader storage", ["STORAGE_DEGRADED", READER_LAYER], ...]` arm and its siblings — the exact code AND layer assertions DoD 4 requires
  :286 the remaining `readProductContractRevision` driver
MOVE, do not COPY. Two suites asserting the same arm means a later edit fixes one and leaves the other, and the duplicate reads as coverage. After the move, `grep -n readProductContractRevision product-contract-revision-store.test.ts` should return only what genuinely belongs to the WRITER's story (e.g. a write-then-read round trip that is really about the write).
(b) The new suite must DRIVE THE PRODUCTION READER over a real file-backed SQLite store — never a reimplementation, never a mock decoder. Keep the `decodeProductContractRevisionBytes` spy shape from store.test.ts:32-34 if the moved arms rely on it, so the "composes the core codec, never reimplements it" assertion (DoD 2) travels with them.
(c) RE-RUN THE GATE AND QUOTE IT: `(cd apps/daemon && pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/runtime-entrypoint.test.ts)` must report `missing: [], unexpected: [], wrongContent: []`. That exact object is the evidence — an exit code alone is not, and the gate reports BY NAME precisely so a regression says which module.

(d) DoD 5, THE CONSUMER EDGE — record it in a row comment, do not invent a call site. Name task-db1a8566958f416b92105cc2c7e51591 as the consumer that will compose this reader, with its id. This row lands the PRODUCER slice and taskRail 3 forbids it satisfying that row's resolver DoD, so clause (a) of the pure-package rail — naming the consumer task — is the correct discharge here, not clause (b).

(e) GATES, each FOREGROUND, UNPIPED, ALONE. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` quoting its `$ tsc` echo; the focused suite over BOTH product-contract revision test files plus runtime-entrypoint.test.ts, quoting `Test Files`/`Tests`. A bare `pnpm test` runs ZERO daemon tests. Repo-wide red path-attributed merge-base vs HEAD, owned-path intersection EMPTY.

amendments.reason: The topology gate is right and the fix is a file split, not a new consumer. Measured at HEAD 62b4d7f6: runtime-entrypoint.test.ts:160 seeds the runtime tier from `file === ENTRY_MODULE || present.has(testSiblingOf(file))` and then propagates only through `relativeImportTargets` over `modules`, which EXCLUDES `.test.ts`. So a module reached only from a test file never joins the tier. `product-contract-revision-reader.ts` has no `reader.test.ts` sibling and no PRODUCTION importer (the store does not import it; only store.test.ts:16 does), so it is test-tier and its `.js` bridge lands in the gate's `unexpected` list. The reader's arms ALREADY EXIST — readback at store.test.ts:194 and the READER_LAYER refusals at :238-:286 — they are simply in the wrong file, which is exactly why the sibling is missing. Splitting them into product-contract-revision-reader.test.ts makes the tier honest, keeps every one of the five untracked files, adds no production cycle, and relieves a 300-line suite. It is NOT gaming the scanner: a writer importing its own reader to satisfy a topology probe would be, and that is explicitly rejected.
